L79: ### ご挨拶
L80: 
L81: 坂田犬猫病院院長　坂田雷太です。
L82: 
L83: 坂田犬猫病院は、犬猫専門病院として、１９９８年に開業しました。
L84: 
L85: 院内には最新の医療機器を完備し、さまざまな症状に最適な医療を施せるよう努めております。
L86: 
L87: 私たちは、ワンちゃん・ネコちゃんの元気で長生きするためのお手伝いをいたします。
L88: 
L89:  坂田犬猫病院には病気にならないためにウェルネスプログラムを提案しています。
L90: 
L91: ウェルネスとは、予防しようとすれば出来る異常は全てなく、細かい異常もない状態と定義されます。
L92: 
L93: そして、言葉が話せない犬猫は特に早期発見早期治療が重要です。
L94: 
L95: ６ヶ月から１年に一度の健康診断は非常に重要です。
L96: 
L97: しかし、突然に症状が現れることもあり、このようなときは、診断・治療を速やかに行わなければなりません。正確な診断をつけてこそ正確な治療が行えます。犬猫は言葉が話せません。
L98: 
L99: 飼い主様もそのための各種検査にご理解ご協力ください。

L14: # The Journey
L15: 
L16: At Animal Cancer Centre our mission is to support you through this challenging time with compassion and care.
L17: 
L18: We are dedicated to guiding you through every step of the journey, offering clear, comprehensive information and personalised support tailored to your pet’s unique needs.
L19: 
L20: Continue reading to learn more about what to expect during your journey.
L21: ### “Cancer is a word, not a sentence”
L22: 
L23: Dr. Robert Buckman, 2006
L24: 
L25: 【11†Image: Animal Cancer Vet】
L26: 
L27: Step 1
L28: 
L29: Making an appointment.
L30: 
L31: ACCWA is a specialist referral practice and does not accept primary care consultations. We focus exclusively on patients referred to us for specialised care. If your local veterinarian diagnoses or strongly suspects cancer you may be offered or can request referral to ACCWA. Appointments can be booked before referral information is received.
L32: To minimise the inconvenience and stress of travel to a vet clinic, ACCWA offers minimally invasive Zoom telehealth consultations for most cases, as well as consultation times in the early morning and early evening.
L33: 
L34: Online bookings can be made following this link.
L35: 
L36: Alternatively, you can call on (08) 6556 9901.
L37: The wait-time for initial consultations for non-life threatining conditions may be 2-3 weeks. This allows for urgent and unwell cases to be brought forward and seen sooner. If your pet is unwell or the diagnosis considered urgent, please indicate this to the person making your appointment or on the booking form. Incoming referral cases are reviewed daily and someone from ACCWA will contact you to change your appointment if indicated.
L38: 
L39: Step 2
L40: 
L41: Before your consultation
L42: Before your consultation, one of ACCWA’s registered veterinary nurses will contact you to discuss your pet’s health, treatment goals, and strategies to ensure your pet’s visit is as stress-free as possible. If we can’t reach you on the phone, we will email you a survey to complete and return. This information allows us to understand more about your pet and formulate the best available treatment options.
L43: 
L44: Step 3
L45: 
L46: Initial consultation
L47: Initial consultation are 45 minutes in duration and during this time, you will be provided with a detailed explanation of your pet’s diagnosis, treatment options and expectations.
L48: 
L49: Treatment options are often a combination of medical oncology therapies including in-hospital and at-home chemotherapy, small molecular inhibitors/targeted therapy and immunotherapy, and where required, opinions and collaboration with specialists in surgical and radiation oncology.
L50: Zoom telehealth consults are recorded (with permission) and are available through your pet’s portal.
L51: 
L52: ACCWA also works closely with holistic and palliative care veterinarians.
L53: 
L54: Step 4
L55: 
L56: On the day of treatment
L57: 
L58: ACCWA offers different solutions to help you and your pet through the journey of treatment.
L59: For in-hospital intravenous chemotherapy you will be able to stay with your pet during their assessment and whilst pre-treatment tests are being performed.  Due to the care and time it takes to correctly prescribe and compound intravenous chemotherapy, in most cases there is a delay between the pre-treatment assessment and the treatment being administered. Due to safety reasons, owners are not permitted to stay with their pets during administration of chemotherapy.
L60: Oral chemotherapy can usually be given soon after the assessments are complete so the need to wait and/or for hospitalisation is usually not required.  Alternatively, oral chemotherapy may be administered by an at-home veterinary service or your local veterinarian.
L61: 
L62: All day hospitalisation is available for convenience and will be required if your pet is booked for a procedure or requires sedation for treatment.
L63: 
L64: Our Community
L65: 
L66: After treatment
L67: We are here to be the family you never thought you would need.
L68: 
L69: Regardless of whether treatment was last week or last year, you and your pet remain part of the ACCWA community.  Pets that develop recurrence or progression of their disease are not required to obtain a new referral but can return directly to ACCWA.
L70: For most pets, the time will come when palliative care is required. Palliative care is the patient-centred care where the primary goal is to optimise the quality of life. Quality of life scales can help you and your family navigate through end-of life decisions.
L71: 
L72: Every pet that undergoes treatment at ACCWA has the potential to contribute to clinical research.  This type of research advances the understanding of disease, treatment options and prognostic factors to benefit the patients of the future.
